cards.title: Context-Dependent PBPK Reporting and Sensitivity Standards
cards.claim: FDA and EMA guidance documents provide nonbinding recommendations for PBPK report content, including sensitivity analysis and parameter justification. These standards apply specifically to PBPK analyses intended to support regulatory decisions or replace clinical data; they are not mandatory for all simple IV simulations or non-regulatory prospective scenarios. The '10-fold' (CYP) and '30-fold' (transporter) sensitivity ranges cited in EMA guidance are illustrative examples of 'worst-case' approaches, not universal project thresholds.
conditions: Applicable when the simulation is a PBPK analysis intended for regulatory submission or high-impact decision support.
Not applicable to simple compartmental IV simulations where no absorption or mechanistic enzyme/transporter modeling is performed.
Source status is EXTERNAL_SOURCE_NOT_PROJECT_POLICY; these are guidelines, not binding project rules.
required_inputs: Explicit definition of the simulation's intended use (regulatory vs. exploratory).
Identification of the model type (PBPK vs. simple compartmental).
Source-specific justification for any sensitivity ranges used (e.g., literature variability vs. worst-case assumption).
limitations: Guidance documents do not validate specific models or specify project-specific dose levels.
Illustrative fold-change ranges cannot be applied universally to all parameters or all simulation types.
Abstract-only or partial excerpts do not constitute full methodological validation.
cards.downstream_use: Determine whether full PBPK reporting standards (e.g., platform qualification, detailed parameter sourcing) are required for the current simulation task. If the simulation is not PBPK-based or not for regulatory submission, simplified reporting may be acceptable per project draft policy.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Sensitivity analyses and evidence-supported regimen/formulation feasibility

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
